subject.title: Feature: Opt-in cross-channel visibility in TUI (mirror iMessage/Telegram activity)

question: Should OpenClaw add a default-off TUI cross-channel observe or mirror mode, and what transcript visibility boundary should it enforce across agents, sessions, channels, devices, and operators?
rationale: The code has Gateway event primitives that could support observation, but exposing cross-channel transcripts changes product scope, privacy expectations, and likely public CLI/config surface.

options.title: Read-only observer first
options.body: Add a default-off `openclaw tui --observe` style mode that only shows authorized activity for a selected agent/session scope and defers bidirectional delivery mirroring.

options.title: Full bidirectional mirroring
options.body: Allow TUI and channel messages to appear across surfaces, but require explicit delivery, authorization, redaction, and upgrade policy before implementation.

options.title: No core mirror mode
options.body: Keep logs, selected-session live tailing, or a future activity timeline as the supported monitoring paths and avoid a core cross-channel TUI mirror feature.

recommendation.title: Read-only observer first
recommendation.body: Add a default-off `openclaw tui --observe` style mode that only shows authorized activity for a selected agent/session scope and defers bidirectional delivery mirroring.

likelyOwner.reason: The TUI isolation behavior and recent TUI lifecycle changes route through this account, making it the best available owner for the visibility policy decision.
